text: WHAT'S NEW NO LONGER CUTS A NOTICE'S NAME, in the three ways it was cutting them. (1) The two-line clamp is gone: a citizen deciding whether a notice concerns them has only the title to go on, and the list was showing "EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) FOR RATE OF INTEREST FOR INVESTMENT OF AN…" on the desktop column and a six-line name as two lines on a phone. Titles wrap in full and the rows take the height they need; the list is bounded by how many rows it shows, not by clipping each one. (2) A tender whose name the register lost no longer takes one of the five slots. Fifty-three tender titles stop at the twelfth character, and the cut is in the Department's own record — dosje.gov.in serves the same twelve characters as the page title, the slug was made from them and the attached document is called "tender-document-42-1.pdf" — so nothing can recover the name. Two of the five most recent tenders here were "Annual Contr…" and "Appointment…". They keep their place in the full register at /website/tenders, where the ellipsis says the name was cut. (3) The home tender list now dedupes as that register does: with the unnamed tenders out of the way, two identical "Appointment as Internal Auditors … NBCFDC" notices of 4 February 2026 surfaced side by side.
